nodes.summary: Creates the cycle table of a User's planning Cycles with Delivery date, time window and end date at most 14 days later; status is derived, not stored.

tour.title: What Dandori Is
tour.description: Start with the README and the product vision. Dandori is a meal-planning co-pilot for a few invited Users, each cooking for themselves: cook once and eat three times, plan one grocery delivery (a Cycle) at a time, let Today say what to do next, and let the agent propose changes that the User approves. The README also covers the stack (Go, templ, htmx, Postgres with pgvector on Supabase, and Claude), the v2 status and how `mise run dev` starts the app locally.

tour.title: The Domain Language
tour.description: Before reading any code, learn the vocabulary. GLOSSARY.md defines the ubiquitous language (Cycle, Delivery, Slot, Recipe, Portion, Kitchen Ledger, Profile, Target, Run, Trace) and the rules that govern planning, stock and Runs. Every package name, type and UI label in the later steps uses these terms, and AGENTS.md describes how work on the codebase is organised: per-issue branches off v2 and the two test seams.

tour.title: The Single Binary Entry
tour.description: cmd/dandori/main.go is where the process starts. Its `serve` command reads the environment, chooses a real Claude, demo or absent LLM for agent Runs, sets up OpenTelemetry, applies database migrations and serves the app with graceful shutdown. Its `healthcheck` command probes /healthz, so the container image needs no extra tools to check itself.

tour.title: Composition Root and Features
tour.description: main.go hands off to internal/app/app.go, the file with the widest reach in the graph. It builds every feature Service over one Postgres pool, runs the ledger scheduler on the app clock, and registers every route behind sign-in, language-choice, kitchen-catch-up and tracing middleware. ADR-0006 explains the layout you will see from here on: one package per feature (internal/kitchen, internal/recipes, internal/planning, ...), each split into web_ handlers, a Service and a store, with shared machinery beneath and a single route table in app.
tour.languageLesson: Go has no dependency-injection framework by convention. A 'composition root' is a single ordinary function that constructs concrete values and passes them into constructors, so the whole object graph is visible in one place and checked by the compiler.

tour.title: Users Share Nothing
tour.description: Every store reaches Postgres through internal/db. db.go opens a traced pgx pool, defines the Querier interface stores share, and applies embedded goose migrations. user.go's AsUser runs each transaction as Supabase's authenticated role with the User's JWT claims, and migration 00002 creates the row-level-secured user table that every owned table references. Together they make ADR-0015's rule, that Users share nothing, a guarantee enforced by the database rather than by each query.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL row-level security attaches a policy (for example `user_id = current_user_id()`) to a table, and the database applies it to every SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE. Setting the role and JWT claims at the start of a transaction scopes all queries inside it without a WHERE clause in each one.

tour.title: The Pure Domain Core
tour.description: internal/domain holds the GLOSSARY's rules as plain Go with no I/O: callers load state in and persist the answers it returns. It is the most depended-upon package in the graph. ingredient.go defines Units, Storage Locations and Nutrition, slot.go defines eating-occasion Slots and their times, and cycle.go derives whether a Cycle is upcoming, current or closed from its Delivery. Keeping these rules pure is what lets them be tested directly at Seam-2.

tour.title: The Kitchen Ledger
tour.description: The kitchen is not a table of current stock. Under ADR-0013 it is an append-only log of Movements, and stock is computed by adding them up. domain/ledger.go does that arithmetic (Quantities in tenths, Causes, Counts), the movement migration stores the log, and ledger/service.go is the single write path: it locks a User's kitchen, saves Movements and brings the kitchen up to now on each request and on the scheduler's beat. ADR-0019 explains why the ledger sits in its own package below every feature that writes Movements.

tour.title: One Feature End to End
tour.description: The Kitchen feature shows the handler, Service and store pattern from Step 4 in use. web_handlers.go serves the Kitchen page and its sheets and parses forms, service.go computes kitchen Contents from the Ledger of Step 7 and records Counts and moves while holding the kitchen lock, and web_views.templ renders the inventory by Storage Location. web_messages.go holds every English and Italian string the pages show, mapping each ledger Cause to readable text. The other features (ingredients, recipes, profile, planning, today) follow the same shape.
tour.languageLesson: templ files compile to Go functions: each `templ Name(args)` becomes a type-checked component, so a view's inputs are ordinary Go types and a missing field is a compile error, not a blank in the rendered page.

tour.title: Pages, htmx and Answers
tour.description: Every page renders inside layout.templ's shell: the masthead, the bottom tabs or desktop rail, htmx and the service worker. ADR-0009 puts hx-boost on the body so every link and form works as a plain browser request, and swaps fragments only where keeping the User's place in a list matters. answer.go makes that uniform: a write returns an htmx fragment with a floating Notice to htmx, and a redirect or full page to a plain browser, while httpx.go offers the shared helpers that detect partial requests.
tour.languageLesson: htmx's hx-boost turns ordinary links and forms into AJAX requests that swap the page body, so the same server-rendered HTML works with and without JavaScript. The server tells the two apart by the HX-Request header.

tour.title: Design System and Languages
tour.description: Feature views are not styled ad hoc. docs/design.md describes the 'Pixel ledger' design system, components.templ provides the shared headers, fields, buttons, notices and side sheets that every view is built from, and app.css is the single stylesheet holding its colour and spacing tokens. i18n.go defines the bilingual Message type and the middleware that picks each request's Language, which is why the feature catalogues in Step 8 hold both English and Italian.
tour.languageLesson: CSS custom properties declared on :root act as design tokens. Components reference the variables rather than raw values, so the palette or spacing changes in one place.

tour.title: The Hand-Rolled Agent Loop
tour.description: Dandori talks to Claude through its own small agent engine rather than a framework, as ADR-0003 records. brief.go describes what the agent is told for one Run (system prompt, first prompt, tools), loop.go runs the tool-use loop with retries, bounded turns and a Trace Event for every step, and anthropic.go adapts the LLM port to Claude's Messages API with prompt caching. Because the loop depends only on an interface, tests and demos can swap in a fake model.
tour.languageLesson: A Go interface is satisfied implicitly: any type with the right methods implements it. Declaring a small LLM interface in the agent package (a 'port') lets the Claude adapter, the demo LLM and the scripted test fake plug in without the loop knowing which one it has.

tour.title: Runs: Parsing a Recipe
tour.description: This is where the agent loop of Step 11 meets a feature. The Runs Engine starts agent Runs in the background as their User, records their status and Trace Events, and lets pages follow a Trace live or cancel it. Recipe parsing is the first Run kind: service_draft.go starts a Run on pasted text, service_parse.go asks Claude to fill a submit_recipe tool schema and turns the result into a domain Recipe, and the run migration stores Runs, Traces and the Drafts awaiting the User's approval, as in the README's 'the agent proposes, you approve'.

tour.title: Testing at Two Seams
tour.description: docs/agents/testing.md names the two places tests sit: Seam-1 drives the whole app over HTTP, and Seam-2 tests the pure domain from Step 6. apptest.go boots Dandori in-process on a freshly migrated Postgres with a manual clock, a fake Supabase Auth and the scripted fake LLM, and scenario.go layers a Given/When/Then DSL on top that acts as a User. clock.go is the single place the app reads the time, which is what makes a manual clock possible in these tests.

tour.title: Build, CI and Deploy
tour.description: The Dockerfile compiles the single static binary from Step 3 and ships it on a distroless nonroot image with a self-invoked healthcheck. The CI workflow runs `mise run check` with a test database and Playwright, and on a v2 push builds the image, ships compose.yaml and the Caddyfile over SSH, restarts the stack and verifies /healthz over TLS. ADR-0017 records the hosting choice: one binary on a Hetzner VPS behind Caddy, with the Supabase database in Frankfurt to keep data in the EU.
tour.languageLesson: A multi-stage Dockerfile builds in one image (with the Go toolchain) and copies only the compiled binary into a minimal runtime image. A distroless base has no shell or package manager, which shrinks both the image and its attack surface.
